title: Llovía cuando salí
titleEn: It was raining when I left
blurbEn: The most important text in the unit. Two past tenses in the same sentence: one paints the scene, the other moves the story on.
body:
Ayer salí de casa a las ocho. Llovía mucho y no tenía paraguas.

Esperé el autobús veinte minutos. Mientras esperaba, leí los mensajes del teléfono.

Cuando llegó el autobús, ya estaba completamente mojada.

Dentro hacía calor y había mucha gente. Una señora mayor me miró y sonrió.

De repente el autobús paró. El conductor dijo que había un problema.

Bajamos todos y caminé hasta la oficina. Llegué tarde, pero de buen humor.
translationEn:
Yesterday I left home at eight. It was raining hard and I did not have an umbrella.

I waited for the bus for twenty minutes. While I was waiting, I read the messages on my phone.

When the bus arrived, I was already completely soaked.

Inside it was hot and there were a lot of people. An elderly lady looked at me and smiled.

Suddenly the bus stopped. The driver said there was a problem.

We all got off and I walked to the office. I arrived late, but in a good mood.

Llovía.note: The scene, not an event. The rain had no beginning or end in this story — it was simply going on.

salí.note: One completed action at one moment. That is why it is the preterite while 'llovía' is not.

esperaba.note: 'Mientras' almost always brings the imperfecto: it describes what was going on when something else happened.

había.note: The past of 'hay'. Still one form for singular and plural.

phrases.note: Background. Compare 'llovió mucho' — that would mean the rain happened and finished.
The event that interrupts. 'Cuando' + preterite is the thing that happens; the imperfecto around it is the setting.
